subject: PrivCP operator access — SCIM mappings, SAML assertions, and runbook checklist
messages:
From: Elena Petrova <elena@horizon-analytics.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: PrivCP operator access: initial ask and mapping details

Hi Sofia / Ben —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As discussed, we're moving forward with Redwood Private (VPC) for our analytics workloads and need to finalize how operator access + user provisioning will work for our private control plane. High-level asks from our side: 

- Confirm the SCIM attribute contract and whether Redwood supports incremental (delta) SCIM provisioning from our IdP.
- Provide recommended SAML assertion examples (group vs custom attribute) for mapping to Redwood RBAC roles.
- Define the minimal IAM role / permissions for the operator service account that will run automation in our VPC.
- Send an operator onboarding runbook and preferred test plan for a staged cutover.

Attached: a short CSV (placeholder) of the fields we currently send from our IdP. We can adapt. Our IdP is Azure AD; cert rotation cadence is currently 90 days but we can support different timing if needed.

Questions we have now:
1) Does Redwood support JIT provisioning (SAML->SCIM create on first login) or do you require full SCIM provisioning first?
2) Can SCIM endpoints be locked to a fixed IP / CIDR for inbound from our IdP?
3) What audit logs are retained for provisioning events and how far back?

Would like to schedule a short 30-minute technical call to walk through these items and the runbook. Our preferred window: Thu 22 May 09:00-11:00 CEST.

Thanks — looking forward to the checklist so we can align internal stakeholders.

Best,
Elena Petrova
Head of Platform Security
Horizon Analytics

Attachments: privcp_scim_mapping_v1.csv (see column notes)

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 11:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: PrivCP operator access: initial ask and mapping details

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. We're happy to support Azure AD and can do either full SCIM provisioning or a hybrid JIT + SCIM approach. Quick answers first, then a proposed next step: 

- SCIM: Redwood supports both full and delta SCIM. Delta is preferred for reducing churn; we can accept PATCH deltas for group and user updates.
- SAML mapping: we recommend sending both group claims (for RBAC mapping) and a custom attribute (x-redwood-role) for explicit role assertions.
- Operator IAM: we typically ask customers to create a scoped operator service account with three permissions: Read-only control-plane audit, Token minting (scoped), and Limited network admin rights for connector setup. Ben will provide a more concrete list below.
- Audit logs: provisioning events are retained 180 days by default in the Private control plane, with longer retention available as an add-on.

I've attached our sample SCIM attribute mapping CSV (privcp_scim_mapping_v1.csv) with recommended column names. Ben — can you add the minimal role policy and SAML assertion examples in a follow-up?

We can do Thu 22 May 09:30 CEST for a 30-minute session; I've tentatively booked it on the calendar. Agenda: 1) SCIM contract, 2) SAML assertion samples + cert rotation, 3) operator account permissions + runbook handoff.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Platform Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: privcp_scim_mapping_v1.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena@horizon-analytics.com>, sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 08:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: PrivCP operator access: initial ask and mapping details

Elena / team —

Here are the concrete items we use for Private control plane onboarding. TL;DR: we can support JIT create on SAML first-login, but for operator accounts we usually require SCIM onboarding so we can attach fine-grained entitlements.

SCIM contract (recommended):
- User object: id, externalId, userName (email), name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work].value, active (boolean)
- Group object: id, displayName, members[] (value = user.externalId), meta.lastModified
- Delta support: PATCH with bulk replace for group members accepted.

SAML assertion guidance (see attachment saml-assertion-examples.txt):
- Send groups using urn:oid:2.5.4.11 or the vendor-specific claim your IdP uses. Example claim: <saml:Attribute Name="groups">
- Optional: x-redwood-role (single string) to force assignment to a specific RBAC role (e.g., "operator.readonly").
- We canonicalize group names; please avoid including spaces and special chars if possible.

Operator service account minimal permissions (suggested policy):
- controlplane.audit.read (read-only access to provisioning/audit events)
- controlplane.tokens.create (mint ephemeral tokens scoped to operator tasks)
- network.connector.admin (create/validate connector resources limited to configured CIDR)
- secrets.read (scoped to operator-runbook secrets only)

Notes / security controls:
- SCIM endpoint must be HTTPS with client certs supported. We can also lock the endpoint to a list of allowed source IPs.
- Cert rotation: we can accept a 90-day cadence; recommend automating cert rollover with a new metadata endpoint for quick swap.
- Audit retention: we log SCIM create/update/delete with user and requestor metadata; default 180 days as Sofia noted.

Attachments included: saml-assertion-examples.txt (small examples), operator_onboarding_runbook.pdf (runbook draft).

Next steps:
1) Elena — confirm you can expose SCIM with PATCH delta and whether you prefer IP allowlist + client certs.
2) We will publish a short test plan for a staged cutover (create staging org -> sync users -> run smoke tests -> cutover).*

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

--

Thanks all —

This is helpful and aligns with our security requirements. Quick confirmations from Horizon: 
- We can provide delta (PATCH) SCIM and will enable client cert authentication. We will also publish the connector IP ranges for the allowlist during staging.
- We will include both group claims and x-redwood-role for operator-level assertions; our IdP team confirms they can map groups to attributes as suggested.
- Cert rotation: we'll keep 90-day rotation and set up automation for renewals.

Agreed to the operator minimal permission set Ben proposed. Please share the runbook link and the smoke test checklist prior to the call so our ops team can review.

One small ask: can Redwood provide an example audit entry format for a SCIM patch (sample JSON) so we can validate ingestion to our SIEM? If you can attach that to the runbook that would be great.

We are good for the 22 May 09:30 CEST slot for the technical call (your calendar invite showed up) — looking forward to the walk-through.

Best,
Elena Petrova
Head of Platform Security
Horizon Analytics
